messages:

Subject: Meridian adapter — initial tech inputs and asks

Hi Vivek / Karthik,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Meridian is starting scoping work for the Redwood adapter that will let our deployment automation push datasets and inference requests into our customers' VPCs. Before we lock the statement of work, we need a short architecture walk and a proposed canary test plan that shows how Redwood will validate the adapter in a partner-managed environment.

High-level asks from our side:
- A reference architecture diagram showing network flow (customer VPC <-> Redwood Private control plane <-> adapter).
- Auth and key exchange flow (KMS/HSM and temporary creds) — we need to ensure compatibility with our onboarding model.
- A canary test matrix: success criteria, traffic profile, rollback triggers, length of canary window.
- Audit/log retention and how Redwood surfaces per-tenant observability for our ops team.

Attached is a short Meridian requirements summary (meridian-reqs-v1.pdf) — call out anything you need clarified.

Can we target a technical readout this week? We can do 45 minutes.

Best,
Elena
VP, Platform Partnerships
Meridian Consulting

(Attachment: meridian-reqs-v1.pdf)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Meridian adapter — initial tech inputs and asks

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise reference design and the proposed canary matrix (see attachments). Below are the highlights we think will address your asks; I added owners for the items we discussed.

Reference design (attachment: meridian-adapter-spec-v1.pdf):
- Network: adapter runs in customer-managed subnet with egress to Redwood Private control plane over TLS; optional private peering for high-security customers.
- Data plane: inference payloads are proxied through a lightweight adapter sidecar in the customer VPC; no persistent customer data is stored on Redwood-hosted nodes.
- Auth: short-lived certs issued by customer KMS to the adapter; Redwood validates via mutual TLS and client cert authentication. See auth-flow-diagram.png.
- Observability: adapter emits structured audit logs to a customer-accessible S3/GCS bucket plus aggregated traces to Redwood Console; retention can be configured per account.

Canary test matrix (attachment: canary-test-matrix.xlsx):
- Canary window: 72 hours default for production integrations; can be shortened to 24 hours for low-risk pilots.
- Traffic profile: start at 1% of baseline traffic, ramp to 10% with fixed-step increases and end-to-end latency/99th percentile checks.
- Rollback triggers: request error rate > 1% absolute increase, latency P99 > 2x baseline, or QoS regression on a holdout eval set.

Next steps / scheduling:
- Tech readout: propose Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT (45m). Karthik, Jonas — can you join?
- I'll ship the spec + matrix to your S3 link after your confirmation.

Notes: Karthik will own the auth and performance test plan; Jonas will validate operational runbooks and tracing hooks.

Thanks — Vivek
VP, Partnerships & Solutions
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: meridian-adapter-spec-v1.pdf, canary-test-matrix.xlsx, auth-flow-diagram.png)

On Mon, May 18, 2026 at 10:05 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise reference design and the proposed canary matrix (see attachments).

Quick technical notes from my side (Karthik):
- Auth: mutual TLS + short-lived certs is our preferred pattern. For customers requiring HSM-backed keys, we can support signed challenge tokens (we have an HSM integration pattern). We'll need a Meridian contact who owns KMS/HSM provisioning.
- Caching & batching: adapter should support prefix caching to avoid repeated cold-start KV loads. We'll expose batching knobs in the adapter config so Meridian can tailor latency/cost tradeoffs per customer.
- Model variants & graceful fallback: plan to route to a lower-cost quantized variant if latency spikes or if a region is degraded. Tests should include fallback correctness checks.
- SLO targets to validate in canary: API p95 < 150ms, p99 < 350ms for 512-token requests under 10 RPS baseline. Load test profiles are in the canary workbook.
- Security/compliance: we will emit a signed audit bundle (daily) with the following fields: request id, tenant id, model id, timestamp, and signature.

I'll prepare a short supplemental doc with exact TLS handshake steps and the minimal IAM role template.

—Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Two clarifications from our security team:
- Audit retention: default 90 days is OK for pilots, but enterprise customers may require 7 years. Can Redwood support configurable retention per tenant and export to long-term archival?
- Canary window: for regulated customers we need at least 7 days of telemetry in the canary to capture edge cases. Will that be a configurable option?

We'll also attach an updated requirements doc that includes our KMS/HSM expectations and a short list of pilot customers' network constraints. See attached meridian-reqs-v2.pdf.

Schedule: Wed 2026-05-20 10:00 PT works for us. Please send a calendar invite and agenda.

Best,
Elena
